body.text: athāto dharmajijñāsā //
body.translated_text: Now, therefore, [commences] the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: loke yeṣv artheṣu prasiddhāni padāni, tāni sati saṃbhave tadarthāny eva sūtreṣv ity avagantavyam / na adhyāhārādibhir eṣāṃ parikalpanīyo 'rthaḥ paribhāṣitavyo vā / evaṃ hi vedavākyāny eva ebhir vyākhyāyante / itarathā vedavākyāni vyākhyeyāni svapadārthāś ca vyākhyeyāḥ / tad yatnagauravaṃ prasajyeta /
body.translated_text: Words that are well-known in ordinary usage with respect to [certain] objects — when it is possible, those [words] are to be understood in those very meanings in the <s>sūtras</s>. Their meaning should not be constructed through <s>adhyāhāra</s> (supplying missing words) and the like, nor should it be technically defined. For thus it is Vedic sentences themselves that are explained by these [<s>sūtras</s>]. Otherwise, [both] the Vedic sentences would need explanation and the meanings of the <s>sūtra</s>-words themselves would need explanation — and that would incur the fault of excessive effort (<s>yatnagaurava</s>).

body.text: tatra loke 'yam athaśabdo vṛttād anantarasya prakriyārtho dṛṣṭaḥ / na ceha kiñcid vṛttam upalabhyate / -- bhavitavyaṃ tu tena, yasmin saty anantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā avakalpate / tathā hi prasiddhapadārthakaḥ sa kalpito bhavati / tat tu vedādhyayanam / tasmin hi sati sā avakalpate / -- naitad evam / anyasyāpi karmaṇo 'nantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā yuktā, prāg api ca vedādhyayanāt /
body.translated_text: There, in ordinary usage, the word '<s>atha</s>' is seen as denoting the commencement of what is immediately subsequent to something already accomplished. But here no prior [activity] is perceived. — There must, however, be one, upon whose completion the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> becomes appropriate. For thus [the word '<s>atha</s>'] would have a well-known meaning. That [prior activity] is Vedic study (<s>vedādhyayana</s>). For when that is accomplished, the inquiry becomes appropriate. — [Objection:] This is not so. <s>Dharma</s>-inquiry can be appropriate after some other activity as well, and even before Vedic study.

body.text: ucyate: tādṛśīṃ tu dharmajijñāsām adhikṛtya athaśabdaṃ prayuktavān ācāryaḥ, yā vedādhyayanam antareṇa na saṃbhavati / katham ? vedavākyānām anekavidho vicāra iha vartiṣyate / api ca naiva vayam iha vedādhyayanāt pūrvaṃ dharmajijñāsāyāḥ pratiṣedhaṃ śiṣmaḥ / na hy etad ekaṃ vākyaṃ purastāc ca vedādhyayanād dharmajijñāsāṃ pratiṣedhiṣyati, parastāc ca ānantaryaṃ prakariṣyati / bhidyeta hi tathā vākyam anyā hi vacanavyaktir asya purastād vedādhyayanād dharmajijñāsāṃ pratiṣedhataḥ, anyā ca parastād ānantaryam upadiśataḥ / "vedān adhītya" ity ekasyāṃ vidhīyate 'nūdya ānantaryaṃ, viparītam anyasyām / arthaikatvāc ca ekavākyatāṃ vakṣyati / kiṃ tv adhīte vede dvayam āpatati, gurukulāc ca samāvartitavyaṃ vedavākyāni ca vicārayitavyāni / tatra "gurukulān mā samāvartiṣṭa ; kathaṃ nu vedavākyāni vicārayet ?" ity evamartho 'yam upadeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: It is said [in reply]: The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher, i.e. <s>Jaimini</s>) used the word '<s>atha</s>' with reference to that kind of <s>dharma</s>-inquiry which is not possible without Vedic study. How so? Because a manifold examination of Vedic sentences will be conducted here [in this <s>śāstra</s>]. Moreover, we do not teach here a prohibition of <s>dharma</s>-inquiry prior to Vedic study. For this single sentence cannot both prohibit <s>dharma</s>-inquiry before Vedic study and establish sequential priority after it. For then the sentence would be split — one utterance-form being that which prohibits [inquiry] before Vedic study, and another that which teaches sequence after it. And [<s>Jaimini</s>] will state [later] that unity of sentence arises from unity of meaning. However, when the <s>Veda</s> has been studied, two [duties] present themselves: one must return from the <s>guru</s>'s house (<s>samāvartana</s>), and one must examine Vedic sentences. There [the <s>sūtra</s> means]: 'Do not return from the <s>guru</s>'s house [yet]; how else shall one examine the Vedic sentences?' — this is the purport of the instruction.

body.text: yady evaṃ, na tarhi vedādhyayanaṃ pūrvaṃ dharmajijñāsāyāḥ / evaṃ hi samāmananti "vedam adhītya snāyāt" iti / iha ca vedam adhītya snāsyan dharmaṃ jijñāsamāna imam āmnāyam atikrāmet / na ca āmnāyo nāma atikramitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, then Vedic study is not [required as] prior to <s>dharma</s>-inquiry. For they recite the traditional prescription (<s>āmnāya</s>): 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should bathe [i.e., complete the <s>snāna</s> graduation rite].' And here, one who, having studied the <s>Veda</s> and being about to bathe while desiring to know <s>dharma</s>, would transgress this <s>āmnāya</s>. And an <s>āmnāya</s> is not something to be transgressed.

body.text: tad ucyate: atikramiṣyāma imam āmnāyam / anatikrāmanto vedam arthavantaṃ santam anarthakaṃ kalpayema / dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ karmāvabodhanaṃ nāma / na ca tasya adhyayanamātrāt tatrabhavanto yājñikāḥ phalaṃ samāmananti / yad api ca samāmananti iva, tatrāpi "dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ syāt" ity arthavādatāṃ vakṣyati / na ca adhītavedasya snānānantaryam etad vidhīyate / na hy atra ānantaryasya vaktā kaścic chabdo 'sti / pūrvakālatāyāṃ hi ktvā smaryate, nānantarye / dṛṣṭārthatā ca adhyayanasya ānantarye vyāhanyeta / lakṣaṇayā tv eṣo ' rthaḥ syāt / na ca idaṃ snānam adṛṣṭārthaṃ vidhīyate / kiṃ tu lakṣaṇayā asnānādiniyamasya paryavasānaṃ vedādhyayanasamakālam āhuḥ "vedam adhītya snāyāt", "gurukulān ma samāvartiṣṭa" ity adṛṣṭārthatāparihārāyaiva /
body.translated_text: To this it is said: We shall transgress this prescription. [For,] not transgressing it, we would be making the <s>Veda</s> — which is meaningful — meaningless. For its purpose is seen to be the cognition of [ritual] action (<s>karmāvabodha</s>). And the venerable ritualists (<s>yājñikas</s>) do not recite a fruit resulting from mere study of it. And even where they seem to recite [a fruit], there too [the treatise] will state: 'In matters of substance-preparation and ritual actions, statements of results (<s>phalaśruti</s>) are <s>arthavāda</s> (glorificatory passages) because of being for the sake of another [i.e., the injunction].' Nor is this [bathing] being enjoined as [the duty] immediately after for one who has studied the <s>Veda</s>. For there is no word here that speaks of immediacy (<s>ānantarya</s>). The affix <s>-ktvā</s> ('having') indicates temporal priority (<s>pūrvakālatā</s>), not immediacy. And the purposefulness of study would be contradicted if immediacy [of bathing] were [insisted upon]. This meaning could be through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). And this bathing is not being enjoined as having an unseen purpose (<s>adṛṣṭārtha</s>). Rather, by indication, they say that the end of the restrictions such as non-bathing etc. coincides with the completion of Vedic study: '<s>vedam adhītya snāyāt</s>' ('having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should bathe') and '<s>gurukulān mā samāvartiṣṭa</s>' ('do not return from the <s>guru</s>'s house') — [these are stated] precisely to avoid [the supposition of] an unseen purpose.

body.text: tasmād vedādhyayanam eva pūrvam abhinirvartya anantaraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavya ity athaśabdasya sāmarthyam / na brūmaḥ "anyasyāpi karmaṇo 'nantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā na kartavyā" iti, kiṃ tu "vedam adhītya tvaritena na snātavyam, anantaraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavyaḥ" ity athaśabdasya arthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, having first completed Vedic study alone, <s>dharma</s> is to be inquired into immediately after — this is the force (<s>sāmarthya</s>) of the word '<s>atha</s>.' We do not say that <s>dharma</s>-inquiry should not be undertaken after some other activity as well; rather, the meaning of the word '<s>atha</s>' is: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should not hasten to bathe; immediately [after study], <s>dharma</s> is to be inquired into.'

body.text: ataḥśabdo vṛttasya apadeśako hetvarthena, yathā "kṣemasubhikṣo 'yaṃ deśaḥ, ato 'ham asmin deśe prativasāmi" iti / evam "adhīto vedo dharmajijñāsāyāṃ hetur jñātaḥ, anantaraṃ dharmo jijñāsitavyaḥ" ity ataḥśabdasya sāmarthyam / dharmāya hi vedavākyāni vicārayitum anadhītavedo na śaknuyāt / ataḥ, etasmāt kāraṇāt, anantaraṃ dharmaṃ jijñāsitum icched ity ataḥśabdasya arthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The word "<s>ataḥ</s>" (therefore/after this) indicates what has been completed, with a causal sense, as in: "This country has security and abundance of food; therefore I reside in this country." In the same way, the import of the word "<s>ataḥ</s>" is: "The <s>Veda</s> has been studied, [and thus] the cause for the desire to know <s>dharma</s> has been recognized; immediately after, <s>dharma</s> is to be inquired into." For without having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one would not be able to examine the Vedic sentences for the sake of <s>dharma</s>. Therefore—from this cause—one should wish to inquire into <s>dharma</s> immediately after: this is the meaning of the word "<s>ataḥ</s>."

body.text: dharmāya jijñāsā dharmajijñāsā / sā hi tasya jñātum icchā / sa punaḥ kathaṃ jijñāsitavyaḥ ? ko dharmaḥ, kathaṃlakṣaṇaḥ, kāny asya sādhanāni, kāni sādhanābhāsāni, kiṃparaś ca iti / tatra ko dharmaḥ, kathaṃlakṣaṇa ity ekenaiva sūtreṇa vyākhyātaṃ "codanalakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ" iti1 / kāny asya sādhanāni, kāni sādhanābhāsāni, kiṃparaś ca iti śeṣalakṣaṇena vyākhyātam 2 / kva puruṣaparatvaṃ kva vā puruṣo guṇabhūta ity etāsāṃ pratijñānāṃ piṇḍasya etat sūtram "athāto dharmajijñāsā" iti / dharmaḥ prasiddho vā syād aprasiddho vā / sa cet prasiddho, na jijñāsyaḥ / athāprasiddho, natarām / tad etad anarthakaṃ dharmajijñāsāprakaraṇam /
body.translated_text: The desire (<s>jijñāsā</s>) directed toward <s>dharma</s> is <s>dharmajijñāsā</s>. It is the wish to know it [i.e., <s>dharma</s>]. But how is it to be inquired into? [By asking:] What is <s>dharma</s>? What are its defining characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>)? What are its valid means of knowledge (<s>sādhana</s>)? What are the pseudo-means (<s>sādhanābhāsa</s>)? And what is its ultimate purpose? Among these, "What is <s>dharma</s>?" and "What are its defining characteristics?" are explained by a single <s>sūtra</s>: "<s>Dharma</s> is that purpose which is characterized by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction)." "What are its means, what are the pseudo-means, and what is its purpose?" are explained by the remaining body of <s>sūtras</s>. Where the person is primary, and where the person is subordinate—this <s>sūtra</s>, "<s>Athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>," is the summary of these theses as a whole. Now, <s>dharma</s> is either well-known or not well-known. If it is well-known, there is no need to inquire into it. If it is not well-known, all the more so [there is no need, since inquiry is impossible]. Therefore, this treatise on the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> is purposeless.

body.text: athavā arthavat / dharmaṃ prati hi vipratipannā bahuvidaḥ / kecid anyaṃ dharmam āhuḥ, kecid anyam / so 'yam avicārya pravartamānaḥ kaṃcid eva upādadāno vihanyeta anarthaṃ ca ṛcchet / tasmād dharmo jijñāsitavyaḥ / sa hi niḥśreyasena puruṣaṃ saṃyunakti iti pratijānīmahe / tad abhidhīyate :
body.translated_text: Or rather, it is purposeful. For regarding <s>dharma</s>, learned people hold conflicting views. Some declare one thing to be <s>dharma</s>, others declare another. One who acts without careful examination, adopting just any [view], would be thwarted and would incur harm. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is to be inquired into. For we maintain that it connects a person with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). This is now stated:

body.text: codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is that purpose (<s>artha</s>) which is characterized by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction). ||

body.text: codanā iti kriyāyāḥ pravartakaṃ vacanam āhuḥ / ācāryacoditaḥ karomi iti hi dṛśyate / lakṣyate yena, tallakṣaṇam / dhūmo lakṣaṇam agner iti hi vadanti / tayā yo lakṣyate, so 'rthaḥ puruṣaṃ niḥśreyasena saṃyunakti iti pratijānīmahe / codanā hi bhūtaṃ bhavantaṃ bhaviṣyantaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vyavahitaṃ viprakṛṣṭam ity evaṃjātīyakam arthaṃ śaknoty avagamayitum, nānyat kiṃcanendriyam /
body.translated_text: They say that <s>codanā</s> (injunction) is a statement that impels one to action. For it is observed [in ordinary usage]: "Impelled by the teacher, I act." That by which [something] is indicated (<s>lakṣyate</s>) is its defining mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). For they say: "Smoke is the defining mark of fire." That which is indicated by it [i.e., by <s>codanā</s>]—that is the purpose (<s>artha</s>) [referred to in the <s>sūtra</s>], and we maintain that it connects a person with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). For <s>codanā</s> is able to make known an object of such a kind—past, present, future, subtle, hidden, or remote—[which] no other faculty of perception (<s>indriya</s>) whatsoever [can cognize].

body.text: nanv atathābhūtam apy arthaṃ brūyāc codanā, yathā yatkiṃcana laukikaṃ vacanaṃ ṅadyās tīre phalāni santi" iti / tat tathyam api bhavati, vitatham api bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But <s>codanā</s> might speak of a purpose that does not correspond to reality, just as any ordinary statement [such as] "there are fruits on the bank of the river." That [ordinary statement] may be true or may be false.

body.text: ucyate: vipratiṣiddham idam abhidhīyate "bravīti ca vitathaṃ ca" iti / bravīti ity ucyate 'vabodhayati, budhyamānasya nimittaṃ bhavati iti / yasmiṃś ca nimittabhūte saty avabudhyate, so 'vabodhayati / yadi ca codanāyāṃ satyām "agnihotrāt svargo bhavati" ity avagamyate, katham ucyate ṅa tathā bhavati" iti / atha na tathā bhavati, katham avabudhyate / asantam artham avabudhyata iti vipratiṣiddham /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] It is said: This assertion—"it speaks and yet is false"—is self-contradictory. For when it is said "it speaks," what is meant is: "it makes known, it becomes the cause of someone's understanding." And that which, when present as a cause, [enables someone] to understand—that is what "makes known." If, when <s>codanā</s> is present, it is understood that "from the <s>Agnihotra</s>, heaven results," how can it be said "it is not so"? And if it is not so, how can one understand [it]? [To say] "one understands a non-existent object" is self-contradictory.

body.text: na ca śvargakāmo yajeta" ity ato vacanāt saṃdigdham avagamyate "bhavati vā svargo na vā bhavati" iti / na ca niścitam avagamyamānam idaṃ mithyā syāt / yo hi janitvā pradhvaṃsate ṅaitad evam" iti, sa mithyāpratyayaḥ / na caiṣa kālāntare puruṣāntare 'vasthāntare deśāntare vā viparyeti / tasmād avitathaḥ /
body.translated_text: And from the statement "one who desires heaven should sacrifice," what is understood is not something doubtful—[namely,] "heaven may or may not result." And what is understood with certainty cannot be false. For a false cognition is one that, having arisen, is subsequently sublated [with the realization] "this is not so." But this [Vedic cognition] is not contradicted at any other time, in any other person, in any other condition, or in any other place. Therefore, it is not false.

body.text: yat tu laukikaṃ vacanaṃ, tac cet pratyayitāt puruṣād indriyaviṣayaṃ vā, avitatham eva tat / athāpratyayitāt puruṣād anindriyaviṣayaṃ vā, tat puruṣabuddhiprabhavam apramāṇam / aśakyaṃ hi tat puruṣeṇa jñātum ṛte vacanāt / -- aparasmāt pauruṣeyād vacanād avagatam iti cet / - tad api tenaiva tulyam / naivaṃjātīyakeṣv artheṣu puruṣavacanaṃ prāmāṇyam upaiti, jātyandhānām iva vacanaṃ rūpaviśeṣeṣu / -- nanv aviduṣām upadeśo nāvakalpate / upadiṣṭavantaś ca manvādayaḥ / tasmāt puruṣāḥ santo viditavantaś ca / yathā cakṣuṣā rūpam upalabhyata iti darśanād evāvagatam / -- ucyate: upadeśo hi vyāmohād api bhavati / asati vyāmohe vedād api bhavati / api ca pauruṣeyād vacanād "evam ayaṃ puruṣo veda" iti bhavati pratyayo, na "evam ayam artha" iti / viplavate khalv api kaścit puruṣakṛtād vacanāt pratyayaḥ / na tu vedavacanasya mithyātve kiṃcana pramāṇam asti /
body.translated_text: Now, as for a worldly (non-Vedic) statement: if it comes from a trustworthy person and concerns a sense-perceptible object, it is indeed not false. But if it comes from an untrustworthy person, or does not concern a sense-perceptible object, it is born from human intellect and is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). For that [supersensory matter] cannot be known by a person except through [Vedic] statement. — [Objection:] If it is said that it was learned from another human statement — [Reply:] That too is subject to the same [defect]. In matters of this kind, human speech does not attain the status of a valid authority, just as the speech of those born blind [has no authority] regarding particular colors. — [Objection:] But instruction is not possible from the ignorant; and <s>Manu</s> and others did give instruction; therefore, being persons, they did know [these things], just as we understand from direct observation that form is perceived by the eye. — [Reply:] It is said: Instruction can arise from delusion as well. In the absence of delusion, it [i.e., instruction] can also come from the <s>Veda</s>. Moreover, from a human statement, the cognition that arises is "this person knows thus," not "the matter is thus." Indeed, cognition derived from a man-made statement may prove erroneous. But there is no proof whatsoever for the falsity of Vedic statement.

body.text: nanu sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati / pauruṣeyaṃ vacanaṃ vitatham upalabhya vacanasāmānyād vedavacanaṃ mithyety anumīyate / -- na, anyatvāt / na hy anyasya vitathabhāve 'nyasya vaitathyaṃ bhavitum arhati, anyatvād eva / na hi devadattasya śyāmatve yajñadattasyāpi śyāmatvaṃ bhavitum arhati / api ca puruṣavacanasādharmyād vedava canaṃ vitatham ity anumānam / pratyakṣas tu vedavacane pratyayaḥ / na cānumānaṃ pratyakṣavirodhi pramāṇaṃ bhavati / tasmāc codanālakṣaṇo 'rthaḥ śreyaskaraḥ / - evaṃ tarhi śreyaskaro jijñāsitavyaḥ / kiṃ dharmajijñāsayā ? - ucyate: ya eva śreyaskaraḥ, sa eva dharmaśabdenocyate / - katham avagamyate ? - yo hi yāgam anutiṣṭhati, taṃ dhārmika iti samācakṣate / yaś ca yasya kartā, sa tena vyapadiśyate, yathā pācako lāvaka iti / tena yaḥ puruṣaṃ niḥśreyasena saṃyunakti, sa eva dharmaśabdenocyate / na kevalaṃ loke, vede ' pi
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But [falsity] will be [established] by inference based on general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>). Having observed that human statements are false, one infers by analogy with statements in general that Vedic statements too are false. — [Reply:] No, because they are different. For the falsity of one thing does not entail the falsity of another, precisely because they are different. For from the dark complexion of <s>Devadatta</s>, it does not follow that <s>Yajñadatta</s> too must be dark-complexioned. Moreover, the inference that Vedic statement is false due to its similarity with human statement is [merely] an <s>anumāna</s> (inference). But the cognition regarding Vedic statement is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception, i.e., self-evident). And an inference that contradicts direct perception cannot be a valid <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, the object characterized by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is conducive to the highest good (<s>śreyaskara</s>). — [Objection:] If so, it is the <s>śreyaskara</s> that should be inquired into; what is the point of the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>? — [Reply:] That which is conducive to the highest good is indeed denoted by the word <s>dharma</s>. — [Question:] How is this understood? — [Reply:] He who performs a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is called <s>dhārmika</s> (righteous). And whoever is the performer of something is designated by that [action], as [one who cooks is called] a cook, [one who harvests is called] a harvester. Therefore, that which unites a person with the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) is denoted by the word <s>dharma</s>. Not only in worldly usage, but in the <s>Veda</s> also —

body.text:
Q: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ
Q: tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan //
body.translated_text: [Vedic quote:] "By sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice; those were the first <s>dharmas</s> (ordained rites)." //

body.text: iti yajatiśabdavācyam eva dharmaṃ samānanti / ubhayam iha codanayā lakṣyate, artho 'narthaś ca - ko 'rthaḥ? - yo nihśreyasāya jyotiṣṭomādiḥ / - ko 'narthaḥ? - yaḥ pratyavāyāya śyeno vajra inour ity evamādiḥ / tatra anartho dharma ukto mā bhūd ity arthagrahaṇam / - kathaṃ punar asāv anarthaḥ ? - hiṃsā hi sā, sā ca pratiṣiddhā / - kathaṃ punar anarthaḥ kartavyatayā upadiśyate ? - ucyate: naiva śyenādayaḥ kartavyatayā vijñāyante / yo hi hiṃsitum icchet, tasya ayam abhyupāya iti hi teoām upadeśaḥ / "śyenenābhicaran yajeta" iti hi samāmananti, na "abhicaritavyam" iti /
body.translated_text: — thus they recognize <s>dharma</s> as that which is expressible by the word <s>yajati</s> ("he sacrifices"). Both are characterized here by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) — both the beneficial (<s>artha</s>) and the harmful (<s>anartha</s>). — What is the beneficial? — That which is for the highest good, such as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and others. — What is the harmful? — That which leads to adverse consequences, such as [the rites called] <s>Śyena</s> (hawk), <s>Vajra</s> (thunderbolt), and the like. In that case, the mention of "<s>artha</s>" (the beneficial) is to ensure that the harmful is not called <s>dharma</s>. — But how is that [rite] harmful? — For it involves injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>), and that is prohibited. — But how is the harmful taught as something to be performed? — [Reply:] It is said: The <s>Śyena</s> and others are not understood as something that ought to be performed. For the instruction regarding them is merely this: "For one who wishes to injure, this is the means." The tradition records "let one who practices sorcery sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s>" — not "one ought to practice sorcery."

body.text: nanv aśaktam idaṃ sūtram imāv arthāv abhivaditum, codanālakṣaṇo dharmo nendriyādilakṣaṇaḥ, arthaś ca dharmo nānartha iti / ekaṃ hīdaṃ vākyam / tad evaṃ sati bhidyeta / - ucyate: yatra vākyād evārtho 'vagamyate, tatraivam / tat tu vaidikeṣu, na sūtreṣu / anyato 'vatage 'rthe sūtram evamartham ity avagamyate, tena ca ekadeśaḥ sūtryata iti sūtram / tatra bhinnayor eva vākyayor imāv ekadeśāv ity avagantavyam / athavā arthasya sataś codanālakṣaṇasya dharmatvam ucyata ity ekārtham eveti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, this <s>sūtra</s> is incapable of expressing both these meanings — [namely,] that <s>dharma</s> is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) and not by the senses, and that <s>dharma</s> is the beneficial and not the harmful. For this is a single sentence, and in that case it would have to be split. — [Reply:] It is said: [The objection applies only] where the meaning is understood from the sentence alone — that is the case with Vedic [sentences], not with <s>sūtras</s>. When the meaning is understood from elsewhere [i.e., from the context], the <s>sūtra</s> is understood as having that meaning; and [the principle is that] a <s>sūtra</s> captures only a part [of the meaning], hence [the term] <s>sūtra</s> (thread/aphorism). Therefore, it should be understood that these are parts of two separate sentences. Or alternatively, it is said that <s>dharma</s>-hood belongs to what is [already understood as] a beneficial object characterized by <s>codanā</s> — thus [the sūtra] has a single meaning only.

body.text: tasya nimittaparīṣṭiḥ //
body.translated_text: "<s>Tasya nimittaparīṣṭiḥ</s>" — [Sūtra 1.1.2:] The investigation of its means (<s>nimitta</s>). //

body.text: uktam asmābhiḥ "codanānimittaṃ dharmasya jñānam" iti / tat pratijñāmātreṇoktam / idānīṃ tasya nimittaṃ parīkṣiṣyāmahe, kiṃ codanaiva uta anyad api iti / tasmān na tāvan niścīyate "codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharma" iti /
body.translated_text: We have stated that 'knowledge of <s>dharma</s> arises from injunction (<s>codanā</s>).' That was stated merely as a thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>). Now we shall examine its ground (<s>nimitta</s>)—whether it is injunction alone, or something else as well. Therefore, it is not yet determined that '<s>dharma</s> is that which has injunction (<s>codanā</s>) as its defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>).'

body.text: tad ucyate :
body.translated_text: To this it is said:

body.text: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣam animittam, vidyamnānopalambhanatvāt //
body.translated_text: When there is actual contact (<s>satsaṃprayoga</s>) of a person's senses [with their objects], the cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) that arises is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception); it is not a ground [for knowing <s>dharma</s>], because it apprehends only what is present (<s>vidyamāna</s>). //

body.text: idaṃ parīkṣyate: pratyakṣaṃ tāvad animittam / - kim kāraṇam ? - evaṃlakṣaṇakaṃ hi tat: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣam / sati indriyārthasaṃbandhe yā puruṣasya buddhir jāyate, tat pratyakṣam / bhavisyaṃś caiṣo 'rtho na jñānakāle 'sti / sataś caitad upalambhanaṃ, nāsataḥ / ataḥ pratyakṣam animittam /
body.translated_text: This is being examined: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), to begin with, is not a ground [for knowing <s>dharma</s>]. —For what reason?— Because it has the following defining characteristic: 'When there is actual contact of a person's senses [with their objects], the cognition that arises is perception.' When there is a connection between the sense-organ and its object, the cognition that arises in a person—that is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. But <s>dharma</s> is something that will come to be [in the future], and does not exist at the time of cognition. And this [perception] is the apprehension of what exists, not of what does not exist. Therefore, perception is not a ground [for knowing <s>dharma</s>].

body.text: buddhir vā janma vā saṃnikarṣo veti naiṣāṃ kasyacid avadhāraṇārtham etat sūtram / sati indriyārthasaṃprayoge, nāsati ity etāvad avadhāryate / anekasmin avadhāryamāṇe bhidyeta vākyam / pratyakṣapūrvakatvāc ca anumānopamānārthāpattīnām apy akāraṇatvam / abhāvo 'pi nāsti, yataḥ
body.translated_text: Whether [it is called] 'cognition' (<s>buddhi</s>), or 'arising' (<s>janma</s>), or 'contact' (<s>saṃnikarṣa</s>)—this <s>sūtra</s> is not for the purpose of determining any one of these. Only this much is determined: [perception occurs] when there is actual contact of the senses with their objects, not when there is none. If [one tried to] determine multiple [defining features], the statement would be split [into separate propositions]. And since inference (<s>anumāna</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) are preceded by perception, they too are not grounds [for knowing <s>dharma</s>]. Nor does absence (<s>abhāva</s>) [serve as such a ground], because—

body.text: autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam upadeśo 'vyatirekaś ca arthe 'nupalabdhe, tat pramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasya, anapekṣatvāt //
body.translated_text: But the relation of word (<s>śabda</s>) with meaning (<s>artha</s>) is innate (<s>autpattika</s>); the knowledge of that [<s>dharma</s>] is instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>); and there is non-deviation (<s>avyatireka</s>) with respect to the object even when [it is] not [otherwise] apprehended. That is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), [this is the view] of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because it is independent (<s>anapekṣa</s>). //

body.text: autpattika iti nityaṃ brūmaḥ / utpattir hi bhāva ucyate lakṣaṇayā / aviyuktaḥ śabdārthayor bhāvaḥ saṃbandhena, notpannayoḥ paścāt saṃbandhaḥ / autpattikaḥ śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya agnihotrādilakṣaṇasya dharmasya nimittaṃ pratyakṣādibhir anavagatasya / - katham? - upadeśo hi bhavati / upadeśa iti viśiṣṭasya śabdasya uccāraṇam / avyatirekaś ca bhavati tasya jñānasya / na hi tad utpannaṃ jñānaṃ viparyeti / yac ca nāma jñānam utpannaṃ na viparyeti, na tac chakyate vaktuṃ ṅaitad evam" iti, "yathā vijñāyate, na tathā bhavati, yathaitan na vijñāyate, tathaitad" iti / anyad asya hṛdaye, anyad vāci syāt / evaṃ vadato viruddham idam avagamyate "asti nāsti ca" iti / tasmāt tat pramāṇam, anapekṣatvāt / na hy evaṃ sati pratyayāntaram apekṣitavyaṃ puruṣāntaraṃ vā / svayaṃpratyayo hy asau / bādarāyaṇasyedaṃ mataṃ kīrtyate bādarāyaṇaṃ pūjayituṃ, nātmīyaṃ mataṃ paryudasitum /
body.translated_text: 'Innate' (<s>autpattika</s>) we declare to mean 'eternal' (<s>nitya</s>). For 'origination' (<s>utpatti</s>) is figuratively (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) called 'being' (<s>bhāva</s>). The being—i.e., relation—of word and meaning is inseparable; it is not that a relation arises after they have come into being. The innate relation of word with meaning is the ground for [knowing] that <s>dharma</s> characterized by the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, which is not apprehended by perception and other [means]. —How?— Because there is instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). '<s>Upadeśa</s>' means the utterance of a distinguished word [i.e., Vedic injunction]. And there is non-deviation (<s>avyatireka</s>) of that knowledge—for the knowledge once arisen does not go astray. And that which, once a cognition has arisen, does not go astray—it cannot be said of it 'this is not so,' or 'it is not as it is cognized, but rather as it is not cognized.' [Otherwise] one thing would be in his heart and another on his lips. From one who speaks thus, the contradictory [assertion] 'it exists and it does not exist' is understood. Therefore, that [Vedic word] is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), because it is independent (<s>anapekṣa</s>)—for, this being the case, no other cognition nor any other person need be relied upon. For it [the Veda] is self-authenticating (<s>svayaṃpratyaya</s>). The view of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> is cited here in order to honor <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, not in order to set aside one's own view.

body.text: vṛttikāras tv anyathemaṃ granthaṃ varṇayāṃcakāra tasya nimittaparīṣṭir ity evamādim :
body.translated_text: The <s>Vṛttikāra</s> (author of the <s>Vṛtti</s>), however, explained this passage differently, [beginning with] 'the examination of the ground of that [<s>dharma</s>]' and so forth:

body.text: na parīkṣitavyaṃ nimittam / pratyakṣādīni hi prasiddhāni pramāṇāni tadantargataṃ ca śāstram / atas tad api na parīkṣitavyam /
body.translated_text: The ground need not be examined. For perception and the other [means of valid knowledge] are well established, and scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is included within them. Therefore, it too need not be examined.

body.text: nanu vyabhicārāt parīkṣitavyaṃ nimittam / śuktikā hi rajatavat prakāśate yatas, tena pratyakṣaṃ vyabhicarati, tanmūlatvāc ca anumānādīny api / tatrāparīkṣya pravartamāno 'rthād vihanyeta anarthaṃ cāpnuyāt kadācit /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the ground must be examined because of deviation [i.e., error]. For a shell appears like silver; since perception thus deviates, and since inference and the rest are based upon it, they too [are subject to error]. Therefore, one who proceeds without examination would be thwarted in his purpose and might even incur harm.

body.text: naitad evam / yat pratyakṣam, na tad vyabhicarati / yad vyabhicarati, na tat pratyakṣam / - kiṃ tarhi pratyakṭam ? -
body.translated_text: This is not so. That which is [genuine] perception does not deviate. That which deviates is not perception. —Then what is perception?—

body.text: tatsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma sat pratyakṣam /
body.translated_text: When there is actual contact (<s>satsaṃprayoga</s>) of a person's senses [with their objects], the cognition that arises, being veridical (<s>sat</s>), is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

body.text:
yadviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ, tenaiva saṃprayoge indriyāṇāṃ puruṣasya buddhijanma sat pratyakṣam / yad anyaviṣayaṃ jñānam anyasaṃprayoge bhavati, na tat pratyakṣam / - kathaṃ punar idam avagamyate "idaṃ tatsaṃprayoge, idam anyasaṃprayoge" iti ? - yan nānyasaṃprayoge, tat tatsaṃprayoge / etadviparītaṃ anyasaṃprayoga iti / - kathaṃ jñāyate, yadā hi śuktikāyām api rajataṃ manyamano "rajatasaṃnikṛṣṭaṃ me cakṣur" iti manyate? - bādhakaṃ hi yatra jñānam utpadyate ṅaitad evaṃ, mithyājñānam idam " iti, tad anyasaṃprayoge, viparītaṃ tatsaṃprayoga iti / - prāg bādhakajñānotpatteḥ katham avagamyate, yadā na tatkāle saṃyagjñānasya mithyājñānasya ca kaścid viśeṣaḥ? - yadā kṣudādibhir upahataṃ mano bhavati, indriyaṃ vā timirādibhiḥ, saukṣmyādibhir vā bāhyo viṣayas, tato mithyājñānam, anupahateṣu saṃyagjñānam / indriyamanorthasaṃnikarṣo hi jñānasya hetuḥ, asati tasmin ajñānāt / tadantargato doṣo
mithyājñānasya hetuḥ / duṣṭeṣu hi jñānaṃ mithyā bhavati / - katham avagamyate ? - doṣāpagame saṃpratipattidarśanāt / - kathaṃ duṣṭāduṣṭāvagama iti cet, - prayatnena anvicchanto na ced doṣam upalabhemahi, pramāṇābhāvād aduṣṭam iti manyemahi / tasmād yasya ca duṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ yatra ca mithyeti pratyayaḥ, sa eva asamīcīnaḥ pratyayo nānya iti /
body.translated_text: The cognition whose object [is present]—when there is contact of the sense organs of the person with that very [object], the arising of determinate cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). That cognition which has a different object and arises from contact with something else is not <s>pratyakṣa</s>. — But how is this ascertained: 'this [arises] from contact with that [object], this from contact with something else'? — That which does not arise from contact with something else arises from contact with that [object]; the reverse is 'contact with something else.' — How is this known, when even one who perceives silver in a mother-of-pearl shell thinks 'my eye is in contact with silver'? — When a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-jñāna</s>) arises [saying] 'this is not so; this is a false cognition,' that [is known to be] from contact with something else; the reverse is contact with that [object]. — Before the arising of the sublating cognition, how is it ascertained, when at that time there is no difference between correct cognition (<s>samyag-jñāna</s>) and false cognition (<s>mithyā-jñāna</s>)? — When the mind is impaired by hunger etc., or the sense organ by cataract (<s>timira</s>) etc., or the external object by subtlety etc., then there is false cognition; when these are unimpaired, [there is] correct cognition. For the contact of the sense organ, mind, and object is the cause of cognition; in its absence there is no cognition. A defect (<s>doṣa</s>) present within that [contact] is the cause of false cognition. For when [the causes] are defective, the cognition is false. — How is this ascertained? — Because, upon the removal of the defect, correct apprehension is observed. — If asked: how is the knowledge of the defective and the non-defective obtained? — If, upon careful investigation, we do not find a defect, we consider it non-defective due to the absence of evidence [of defect]. Therefore, the cognition of one whose instrument of perception (<s>karaṇa</s>) is defective, and in which there arises [the subsequent judgment] 'this was false'—that alone is the incorrect cognition, not the other.

body.text: nanu sarva eva nirālambanaḥ svapnavat pratyayaḥ / pratyayasya hi nirālambanatā svabhāva upalakṣitaḥ svapne / jāgrato 'pi śtambha" iti vā "kuḍyam" iti vā pratyaya eva bhavati / tasmāt so 'pi nirālambanaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But is not every cognition without external support (<s>nirālambana</s>), like a dream? For the nature of cognition as being without external support is observed in dream. Even for the waking person, there is merely a cognition [of] 'a pillar' or 'a wall.' Therefore, that [waking cognition] too is without external support.

body.text: ucyate: śtambha" iti jāgrato buddhiḥ supariniścitā kathaṃ viparyasiṣyati? - svapne 'py evam eva supariniścitā āsīt prāk prabodhanāt, na tatra kaścid viśeṣa iti cen, - na, svapne viparyayadarśanād aviparyayāc ca itarasmin / - tatsāmānyād itaratrāpi bhaviṣyati iti cet / -- yadi pratyayatvāt svapnapratyayasya mithyābhāvaḥ, jāgratpratyayasyāpi bhavitum arhati / atha pratītis tathābhāvasya hetuḥ, na śakyate "pratyayād ayam anya" iti vaditum / anyatas tu svapnapratyayasya mithyābhāvo viparyayād avagataḥ / - kuta iti cet / - sanidrasya manaso daurbalyān nidrā mithyābhāvasya hetuḥ svapnādau svapnānte ca / suṣuptasya pratyayābhāva eva / acetayan eva hi śuṣupta" ity ucyate / tasmāj jāgrataḥ pratyayo na mithyeti / - nanu jāgrato 'pi karaṇadoṣaḥ syāt ? - yadi syād, avagamyeta / - svapnadarśanakāle 'pi nāvagamyata iti cet / - tan na / prabuddho hy avagacchati ṅidrākrāntaṃ me mana āsīd" iti /
body.translated_text: It is replied: the well-established cognition of the waking person, [such as] 'a pillar'—how will it be overturned? — [Objection:] In dream too, [the cognition] was equally well-established before awakening; there is no difference there. — [Reply:] No, because in dream, reversal (<s>viparyaya</s>) is observed, whereas in the other [waking state], there is no reversal. — [Objection:] Because of their similarity, [reversal] may occur in the other [state] too. — If the falsity of dream cognition is due to its being a cognition [as such], then the falsity of waking cognition too ought to follow. But if the cognition itself is the cause of such [non-existent] being, it cannot be said that one [cognition] is different from another. However, from another [factor], the falsity of dream cognition is ascertained from its reversal. — From what? — From the weakness of the mind affected by sleep; sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is the cause of [cognition's] falsity, at the beginning and end of the dream. In deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>), there is simply the absence of cognition. For one who is unconscious is called 'deeply asleep.' Therefore, the cognition of the waking person is not false. — But could there not be a defect in the instrument [of perception] even for the waking person? — If there were, it would be ascertained. — [Objection:] Even during dream-vision it is not ascertained [at that time]. — That is not so. For the awakened person ascertains: 'my mind was overcome by sleep.'

body.text: śūnyas tu / - katham ? - arthajñānayor ākārabhedaṃ nopalabhāmahe / pratyakṣā ca no buddhiḥ / atas tadbhinnam artharūpaṃ nāma na kiṃcid asti iti paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: [The <s>Śūnyavādin</s> says:] But [all is] empty (<s>śūnya</s>). — How so? — We do not perceive a difference in form (<s>ākāra-bheda</s>) between the object and the cognition. And our cognition is directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Therefore, we see that there is nothing called an 'object-form' (<s>artha-rūpa</s>) that is different from that [cognition].

body.text: syād etad evaṃ, yady arthākārā buddhiḥ syāt / nirākārā tu no buddhiḥ, ākāravān bāhyo 'rthaḥ / sa hi bahirdeśasaṃbaddhaḥ pratyakṣam upalabhyate / arthaviṣayā hi pratyakṣabuddhir na buddhyantaraviṣayā / kṣaṇikā hi sā na buddhyantarakālam avasthāsyata iti / utpadyamānaivāsau jñāyate jñāpayati cārthāntaraṃ pradīpavad iti yady ucyeta, tan na / na hy ajñāte 'rthe kaścid buddhim upalabhate, jñāte tv anumānād avagacchati / tatra yaugapadyam anupapannam / - nanu utpannāyām eva buddhāv artho "jñāta" ity ucyate nānutpannāyām / ataḥ pūrvaṃ buddhir utpadyate, paścāj jñāto 'rthaḥ / - satyam / pūrvaṃ buddhir utpadyate, na tu pūrvaṃ jñāyate / bhavati hi kadācid etad, yaj jñāto 'rthaḥ san "ajñāta" ity ucyate / na ca arthavyapadeśam antareṇa buddhe rūpopalambhanam / tasmān nāvyapadeśyā buddhir, avyapadeśyaṃ ca naḥ pratyakṣam / tasmād apratyakṣā buddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] This would be so if cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) had the form of its object. But cognition, according to us, is formless (<s>nirākāra</s>); it is the external object that possesses form. For that [object], being connected with an external location, is directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Perceptual cognition has the object as its content, not another cognition. For cognition is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) and would not persist for the duration of another cognition. — [Buddhist reply:] If it is said that cognition, at the very moment of arising, is known and also illuminates another object, like a lamp — [Mīmāṃsaka reply:] No. For no one apprehends cognition when the object is not [yet] known; rather, when the object is known, one infers [the existence of cognition]. In that case, simultaneity [of cognition and its apprehension] is impossible. — [Buddhist:] But the object is said to be "known" only when cognition has arisen, not when it has not arisen. Therefore, cognition arises first, and afterward the object is known. — [Reply:] True. Cognition arises first, but it is not known first. For it sometimes happens that an object, though known, is said to be "not known." And there is no apprehension of the form of cognition apart from the designation of the object. Therefore, cognition is not non-designable, and what is non-designable is, according to us, not directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Therefore, cognition is not directly perceived.

body.text: api ca kāmam ekarūpatve buddher evābhāvo, na tv arthasya pratyakṣasya sataḥ / na caikarūpyam / nirākārām eva hi buddhim anumimīmahe, sākāraṃ cārthaṃ pratyakṣam evāvagacchāmaḥ / tasmād arthālambanaḥ pratyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, even if cognition were uniform [i.e., formless], that would entail the non-existence of cognition [as anything determinate], not [the non-existence] of the object which is directly perceived. And there is no uniformity [in cognition, since different cognitions arise from different objects]. For we infer cognition as formless, while we directly perceive the object as possessing form. Therefore, cognition has the [external] object as its support (<s>ālambana</s>).

body.text: api ca niyatanimittas tantuṣv evopādīyamāneṣu paṭapratyayaḥ / itarathā tantūpādāne 'pi kadācid ghaṭabuddhir avikalendriyasya syāt / na caivam asti / tasmān na nirālambanaḥ pratyayaḥ / ato na vyabhicarati pratyakṣam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, cognition [arises] from a determinate cause: the cognition of cloth arises only when threads are being taken up. Otherwise, even when threads are taken up, there would sometimes arise the cognition of a pot for one whose senses are unimpaired. But this does not occur. Therefore, cognition is not without a [corresponding external] support. Hence, <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) does not deviate [from truth].

body.text: anumānaṃ jñātasaṃbandhasya ekadeśadarśanād ekadeśāntare ' saṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe buddhiḥ / tat tu dvividhaṃ pratyakṣatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ ca / tatra pratyakṣatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ yathā dhūmākṛtidarśanād agnyākṛtivijñānam / sāmānyatodṛṣṭasaṃbandhaṃ ca yathā devadattasya gatipūrvikāṃ deśāntaraprāptim upalabhya āditye 'pi gatismaraṇam /
body.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the cognition of an object that is not in sensory contact, [arising] from perceiving one part [of a previously known relation] when the relation [between the two] is already known. It is of two kinds: that whose relation has been observed through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣato dṛṣṭa</s>), and that whose relation has been observed through general similarity (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>). Among these, the relation observed through direct perception is, for example, the cognition of the form of fire from seeing the form of smoke. The relation observed through general similarity is, for example, observing that <s>Devadatta</s> reaches another place preceded by movement, and [from that general observation] recollecting that the sun too has movement.

body.text: śāstraṃ śabdavijñānād asaṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe vijñānam /
body.translated_text: <s>Śāstra</s> (authoritative verbal testimony) is the cognition of an object not in sensory contact, [arising] from the cognition of [Vedic] words.

body.text: upamānam api sādṛśyam asaṃnikṛṣṭe 'rthe buddhim utpādayati, yathā gavayadarśanaṃ gosmaraṇasya /
body.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy) also produces cognition of an object not in sensory contact, through similarity—as, for example, the seeing of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) [produces] the recollection of a cow.

body.text: arthāpattir api dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā 'rtho 'nyathā nopapadyata ity arthakalpanā, yathā jīvato devadattasya gṛhābhāvadarśanena bahirbhāvasya adṛṣṭasya kalpanā /
body.translated_text: <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is also [a valid means]: the postulation of a [new] fact when a seen or heard fact cannot be explained otherwise—as, for example, when <s>Devadatta</s> is alive but not seen at home, one postulates his being outside, which is unseen.

body.text: abhāvo 'pi pramāṇābhāvo ṅāsti" ity asyārthasyāsaṃnikṛṣṭasya / tasmāt prasiddhatvān na parīklitavyaṃ nimittam /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence) too [is a valid means]: it is the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) for [an object] not in sensory contact, [expressed as] "it does not exist." Therefore, since [these six means] are well-established, the cause [of valid cognition, i.e., <s>codanā</s>] need not be further examined.

body.text: nanu pratyakādīny anyāni bhavantu nāma pramāṇāni, śabdas tu na prāmāṇam / - kutaḥ ? -
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Granted that perception and the others may be valid means of knowledge, but verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is not a valid means (<s>pramāṇa</s>). — Why? —

body.text: animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 1.1.4:] [Verbal testimony] is not a valid cause, because what exists can be perceived. ||

body.text: animittam apramāṇaṃ śabdaḥ / yo hy upalambhanaviṣayo nopalabhyate, sa nāsti, yathā śaśasya viṣāṇam / upalambhanāni cendriyāṇi paśvādīnām / na ca paśukāmeṣṭyanantaraṃ paśava upalabhyante / ato neṣṭiḥ paśuphalā / karmakāle ca karmaphalena bhavitavyam / yatkālaṃ hi mardanaṃ, tatkālaṃ mardanasukham / - kālāntare phalaṃ dāsyati iti cet / - na / na kālāntare phalam iṣṭer ity avagacchāmaḥ / - kutaḥ ? - yadā tāvad asau vidyamānā āsīt, tadā phalaṃ na dattavatī / yadā phalam utpadyate, tadāsau nāsti / asatī ca kathaṃ dāsyati ? api ca karmakāla eva phalaṃ śrūyate / "yāgaḥ karaṇam" iti vākyād avagamyate, "karaṇaṃ ced utpannaṃ, kāryeṇa bhavitavyam" iti / pratyakṣaṃ ca phalakāraṇam anyad upalabhāmahe / na ca dṛṣṭe kāraṇe saty adṛṣṭaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyate, pramāṇābhāvāt / evaṃ dṛṣṭāpacārasya vedasya svargādy api phalaṃ na bhavati iti manyāmahe /
body.translated_text: Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is not a valid cause (<s>nimitta</s>), not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). For that which is an object of perception but is not perceived—that does not exist, like the horn of a hare. And the means of perception are the sense-organs of animals and others. But after the <s>Paśukāmeṣṭi</s> sacrifice, cattle are not perceived. Therefore, the sacrifice does not have cattle as its result. And the result of an action must [be present] at the time of the action. For the pleasure of massage is [present] at the time of massage. — [Objection:] "It will give the result at another time." — [Reply:] No. We do not understand [from the Vedic text] that the sacrifice gives its result at another time. — Why? — When it was in existence [i.e., during the performance], it did not give the result. When the result arises, it [the sacrifice] no longer exists. And how can what does not exist give [a result]? Moreover, the result is heard of [in the Veda] at the very time of the action. From the sentence "the sacrifice is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>)," it is understood: "if the instrument has come into being, the effect must [also come into being]." And we perceive another, directly observable cause of the result. And when a perceived cause exists, an unperceived [cause] cannot be postulated, because there is no valid means [to establish it]. Thus, we hold that even heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and other [results] do not arise for the <s>Veda</s>, which has been shown to be erroneous.

body.text: dṛṣṭaviruddham api bhavati kiṃcid vaidikaṃ vacanam / pātracayanaṃ vidhāya āha śa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokaṃ yāti" iti pratyakṣaṃ śarīraṃ vyapadiśati / na ca tat svargaṃ lokaṃ yāti / pratyakṣaṃ hi tad dahyate / na caiṣa "yāti" iti vidhiśabdaḥ / evaṃjātīyakaṃ ca pramāṇaviruddhaṃ vacanam apramāṇam "ambuni majjanty alābūni, grāvāṇaḥ plavante" iti yathā / tatsāmānyād agnihotrādicodanāsv apy anāśvāsaḥ / tasmān na codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, some Vedic statements are contradicted by what is observed. Having prescribed the arrangement of vessels (<s>pātracayana</s>), it declares: "This sacrificer, armed with sacrificial implements, goes directly to the heavenly world" — thus it designates the perceptible body. But that [body] does not go to the heavenly world, for it is visibly burned. Nor is this word "goes" (<s>yāti</s>) an injunctive term. And a statement of this kind that contradicts the means of valid knowledge is not authoritative — just as [the statements] "gourds sink in water, stones float." By analogy with these, there would be no confidence even in the injunctions regarding <s>Agnihotra</s> and other [rituals]. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is not the object characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>).

body.text: autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 1.1.5:] But the relation of the word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>); the knowledge of that [dharma through verbal injunction is valid]. ||

body.text: tuśabdaḥ pakaṃ vyāvartayati / apauruṣeyaḥ śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya agnihotrādilakṣaṇasya arthasya jñānaṃ pratyakṣādibhir anavagamyamānasya / tathā ca codanālakṣaṇaḥ samyakpratyaya iti / pauruṣeye hi sati saṃbandhe yaḥ pratyayaḥ, tasya mithyābhāva āśaṅkyeta / parapratyayo hi tadā syāt / atha śabde bruvati kathaṃ mithyā iti ? na hi tadānīm anyataḥ puruṣād avagamaḥ / "bravīti" ity ucyate "avabodhayati, budhyamānasya nimittam bhavati" iti / śabde cen nimittabhūte svayam avabudhyate, kathaṃ vipralabdhaṃ brūyān ṅaitad evam" iti / na cāsya codanā śyād vā na vā" iti sāṃśayikaṃ pratyayam utpādayati / na ca "mithyaitad" iti kālāntare deśāntare 'vasthāntare puruṣāntare vā punar avyapadeśyaḥ pratyayo bhavati / yo 'py anyapratyayaviparyāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā "atrāpi viparyasiṣyati" ity ānumānikaḥ pratyaya utpadyate, so 'py anena pratyakṣeṇa pratyayena virudhyamāno bādhyate / tasmāc codanālakṣaṇa eva dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: The word "but" (<s>tu</s>) refutes the preceding objection. The relation of the word with its meaning is innate, i.e., not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) — [and this is] the knowledge of that object characterized by <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, which cannot be ascertained through perception and other [means]. Thus, the valid cognition characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>) [is established]. For if the relation were of human origin, the cognition arising from it could be suspected of being false — it would then be dependent on another person's cognition. But when the word itself speaks, how can it be false? For there is then no dependence on any other person for knowledge. "Speaks" means "causes to understand, becomes the occasion for one who is coming to understand." If, when the word is the occasioning cause, one understands by oneself, how could it speak falsely, saying "this is not so"? Nor does the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) produce a doubting cognition such as "it may or may not be so." Nor does a cognition arise at another time, in another place, in another condition, or for another person — one that cannot be explained away — saying "this is false." And the inferential cognition that arises from seeing the error in other cognitions, thinking "here too there will be error" — even that is overridden, being contradicted by this direct cognition. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is indeed that which is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>).

body.text: syād etad evam: naiva śabdasya arthenāsti saṃbandhaḥ, kuto 'sya pauruṣeyatā apauruṣeyatā vā iti / - katham ? - syāc ced arthena saṃbandhaḥ, kṣuramodakaśabdoccāraṇe mukhasya pāṭanapūraṇe syātām, yadi saṃśleṣalakṣaṇaṃ saṃbandham abhipretya ucyate / kāryakāraṇanimittanaimittikāśrayāśrayibhāvayaunādayas tu saṃbandhāḥ śabdasya anupapannā eva iti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] It may be thus: the word simply has no relation with meaning at all — so how can one speak of it being of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) or not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>)? — How so? — If there were a relation with meaning, then upon uttering the words "razor" (<s>kṣura</s>) and "sweetmeat" (<s>modaka</s>), there should be cutting and filling of the mouth respectively — if one intends a relation characterized by physical contact (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>). But relations such as cause and effect, instrument and result, support and supported, and those arising from origin — these are simply impossible for words.

body.text: ucyate: yo 'tra vyapadeśyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tam ekaṃ na vyapadiśati bhavān, pratyāyyasya pratyāyakasya ca yaḥ saṃjñāsaṃjñilakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhas tam iti / - āha: yadi pratyāyakaḥ śabdaḥ, prathamaśrutaḥ kiṃ na pratyāyayati ? - ucyate: sarvatra no darśanaṃ pramāṇam / "pratyāyaka" iti hi pratyayaṃ dṛṣṭvā avagacchāmaḥ, ṅa prathamaśruta" iti prathamaśravaṇe pratyayam adṛṣṭvā / yāvatkṛtvaḥ śrutena "iyaṃ saṃjñā, ayaṃ saṃjñī" ity avadhāritaṃ bhavati, tāvatkṛtvaḥ śrutād arthāvagamaḥ / yathā cakṣur draṣṭṛ na bāhyena prakāśena vinā prakāśayati ity adraṣṭṛ na bhavati /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] The relation that is to be indicated here — that one relation you fail to indicate: namely, the relation of signifier (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and signified (<s>saṃjñin</s>), that is, the relation between what conveys understanding (<s>pratyāyaka</s>) and what is to be understood (<s>pratyāyya</s>). — [Objection:] If the word is a means of conveying understanding, why does it not convey understanding when heard for the first time? — [Reply:] Observation everywhere is our authority. We know the word to be a "conveyer of meaning" by having observed the understanding it produces, not from the first hearing where no understanding was observed. After the word has been heard as many times as is needed to ascertain "this is the designation, this is the designated," from that many hearings comes the understanding of meaning. Just as the eye is the instrument of seeing, not an external [agent]...

body.text: yadi prathamaśruto na pratyāyayati, kṛtakas tarhi śabdasya arthena saṃbandhaḥ / - kutaḥ? - - svabhāvato hy asaṃbandhāv etau śabdārthau / mukhe hi śabdam upalabhāmahe, bhūmāv artham / "śabdo 'yaṃ na tv arthaḥ, artho 'yaṃ na śabda" iti ca vyapadiśanti / rūpabhedo 'pi bhavati / "gaur" iti imaṃ śabdam uccārayanti, sāsnādimantam artham avabudhyante / pṛthagbhūtayoś ca yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, sa kṛtako dṛṣṭo, yathā rajjughaṭayor iti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If the word does not convey understanding when heard for the first time, then the relation of the word with its meaning is manufactured (<s>kṛtaka</s>). — Why? — Because by their very nature, word (<s>śabda</s>) and meaning (<s>artha</s>) are unrelated. For we perceive the word in the mouth and the meaning on the ground. People distinguish them saying, "This is a word, not a thing" and "This is a thing, not a word." There is also a difference in form: they utter the word <s>gauḥ</s> (cow), but understand the thing possessing a dewlap and so forth. And the relation between things that are distinct is seen to be manufactured — like that of a rope and a pot.

body.text: atha "gaur" ity atra kaḥ śabdaḥ ? - gakāraukāravisarjanīyā iti bhagavān upavarṭaḥ / śrotragrahaṇe hy arthe loke śabdaśabdaḥ prasiddhaḥ / te ca śrotragrahaṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, in <s>gauḥ</s>, what is the word? — The letters <s>ga</s>, <s>au</s>, and <s>visarjanīya</s> (ḥ), says the venerable <s>Upavarṣa</s>. For the term "word" (<s>śabda</s>) is well-known in the world for that which is grasped by the ear. And these [letters] are grasped by the ear.

body.text: yady evam, arthapratyayo nopapadyate / - katham ? - ekaikākṣaravijñāne hy artho nopalabhyate / na ca akṣaravyatirikto 'nyaḥ kaścid asti samudāyo nāmna, yato 'rthapratipattiḥ syāt / yadā hi gakāro, na tadā aukāravisarjanīyau / yadā aukāravisarjanīyau, na tadā gakāraḥ / ato gakārādivyatirikto 'nyo gośabdo 'sti, yato 'rthapratipattiḥ syāt / antarhite 'pi śabde smaraṇād arthapratyaya iti cen, - na / smṛter api kṣaṇikatvād akṣarais tulyatā /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If that is so, the cognition of meaning is not tenable. — How? — For in the knowledge of each individual letter, the meaning is not apprehended. Nor is there any aggregate apart from the letters, called a 'name,' from which comprehension of meaning could arise. For when 'ga' [is present], 'au' and <s>visarga</s> are not; when 'au' and <s>visarga</s> [are present], 'ga' is not. Therefore, there is no word 'go' apart from 'ga' and the rest, from which comprehension of meaning could arise. If [one says] that even when the word has disappeared, cognition of meaning [arises] from memory — no, because memory too, being momentary, is on the same footing as the letters.

body.text: pūrvavarṇajanitasaṃskārasahito 'ntyo varṇaḥ pratyāyaka ity adoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] The last letter, accompanied by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by the preceding letters, is what conveys [the meaning] — thus there is no fault.

body.text: nanv evam api "śabdād arthaṃ pratipadyāmaha" iti laukikaṃ vacanam anupapannaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But even so, the ordinary statement 'we understand meaning from words' would be untenable.

body.text: ucyate: yadi nopapadyate, anupapannaṃ nāma / na hi laukikaṃ vacanam anupapannam ity etāvatā pratyakṣādibhir anavagamyamāno 'rthaḥ śakyo 'bhyupagantum / laukikāni vacanāny upapannārthāny anupapannārthāni ca dṛśyante, yathā "devadatta, gām abhyāja" ity evamādīni "daśa dāḍimāni ṣaḍ apūpā" ity evamādīni ca / - nanu ca śāstrakārā apy evam āhuḥ "pūrvāparībhūtaṃ bhāvam ākhyātenācaṣṭe 'vrajati, pacati' ity upakramaprabhṛty apavargaparyantam" iti yathā / - na śāstrakāravacanam apy alam imam artham apramāṇakam upapādayitum /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] It is said: If it is untenable, then so be it — let it be called untenable. For merely because an ordinary statement is untenable, a meaning not ascertained by perception and other [means of knowledge] cannot be accepted. Ordinary statements are seen to have both valid and invalid meanings — for example, those like '<s>Devadatta</s>, drive the cow!' and those like 'ten pomegranates, six cakes.' — [Objection:] But the authors of treatises (<s>śāstrakāras</s>) too say the same, as for instance: 'A verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>) denotes an event (<s>bhāva</s>) that has a prior and a posterior, from inception to completion, [as in] "he goes," "he cooks."' — [Reply:] Even the statement of a treatise-maker is not sufficient to establish this meaning which lacks independent authority (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

body.text: api ca naivaitad anupapannārtham / akṣarebhyaḥ saṃskāraḥ, saṃskārād arthapratipattir iti bhavanty arthapratipattāv akṣarāṇi nimittam / gauṇa eṣa śabda iti cet, - na gauṇo 'kṣareṣu nimittabhāvaḥ, tadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt / athāpi gauṇaḥ syāt, na "gauṇaḥ śabdo mā bhūd" ity etāvatā pratyakṣādibhir anavagamyamāno 'rthaḥ śakyaḥ parikalpayitum / na hy "agnir māṇavaka" ity ukte 'gniśabdo gauṇo mā bhūd iti "jvalana eva māṇavaka" ity adhyavasīyate / na ca pratyakṣo gakārādibhyo 'nyo gośabda iti, bhedadarśanābhāvād abhedadarśanāc ca / gakārādīni hi pratyakṣāṇi / tasmād "gaur" iti gakārādivisarjanīyāntaṃ padam akṣarāṇy eva / na tebhyo vyatiriktam anyat padaṃ nāma iti / nanu saṃskārakalpanāyām apy adṛṣṭakalpanā / - ucyate: śabdakalpanāyāṃ sā ca śabdakalpanā ca / tasmād akṣarāṇy eva padam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, this [ordinary statement] is not of invalid meaning either. From the letters arises an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>); from the impression arises the comprehension of meaning — thus the letters are the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) in the comprehension of meaning. — If [it is said:] this is a secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) [usage of] the word [i.e., it is only figuratively that letters are said to convey meaning] — [Reply:] No, the causal role of the letters is not secondary, because [meaning] is present when they are present and absent when they are absent. Even if it were secondary, one cannot, merely because 'the word is secondary,' fabricate a meaning not ascertained by perception and other [means]. For when it is said 'the boy is fire,' one does not determine that 'the word "fire" should not be secondary, [so] the boy must be actual flame.' And the word 'go' (cow) is not directly perceived as something other than 'ga' etc., because no difference is observed [between the word and its letters], and because identity is observed. For 'ga' etc. are directly perceived. Therefore, [in] the word '<s>gauḥ</s>' — a <s>pada</s> (word-unit) ending with 'ga,' 'au,' and <s>visarga</s> — it is just the letters [themselves]. There is no other entity called a <s>pada</s> apart from them. — [Objection:] But in postulating impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) too, there is postulation of something unobserved (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). — [Reply:] It is said: In postulating [a separate] word-entity, there is that [postulation of the unobserved] as well as the postulation of the word-entity itself. Therefore, the letters alone are the word (<s>pada</s>).

body.text: atha "gaur" ity asya śabdasya ko 'rthaḥ? - sāsnādiviśiṣṭā ākṛtir iti brūmaḥ / - nanv ākṛtiḥ sādhyāsti vā na veti ? - na pratyakṣā satī sādhyā bhavitum arhati / "rucakaḥ, svastiko, vardhamānaka" iti hi pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate / - vyāmoha iti cet, - na / nāsati pratyayaviparyāse "vyāmoha" iti śakyate vaktum /
body.translated_text: Now, what is the meaning of the word '<s>gauḥ</s>' (cow)? — We say: it is the <s>ākṛti</s> (universal form) characterized by a dewlap (<s>sāsnā</s>) and the like. — [Objection:] But is <s>ākṛti</s> something that needs to be established, or not? — [Reply:] Being directly perceived, it cannot require establishment. For [shapes like] '<s>rucaka</s>' (bracelet), '<s>svastika</s>,' and '<s>vardhamānaka</s>' (the expanding pattern) are directly perceived. — If [it is said:] this is delusion (<s>vyāmoha</s>) — [Reply:] No. In the absence of a reversal of cognition, one cannot say 'it is delusion.'

body.text:
asaty apy arthāntara evaṃjātīyake bhavati pratyayaḥ "paṅktir , yūthaṃ, vanam" iti yatheti cet, - na / asaṃbaddham idaṃ vacanam upanyastam / kim "asati vane vanapratyayo bhavati" iti pratyakṣam eva ākṣipyate "vṛkṣā api na santi" iti ? yady evaṃ, pratyuktaḥ sa mahāyānikaḥ pakṣaḥ / atha kim ākṛtisadbhāvavādy upālabhyate śiddhāntāntaraṃ te duṣyati ; vane 'pi te 'sati vanapratyayaḥ prapnoti" iti / evam api prakṛtaṃ dūṣayitum aśaknuvatas te siddhāntāntaradūṣaṇaṃ nigrahasthānam āpadyate, asādhakatvāt / sa hi vakṣyati "duṣyatu, yadi duṣyati ; kiṃ tena duṣṭena aduṣṭena vā prakṛtaṃ tvayā sādhitaṃ bhavati madīyo vā pakṣo dūṣito bhavati ?" iti / na ca vṛkṣavyatiriktaṃ vanaṃ yasmān nopalabhyate, tato "vanaṃ nāsti" ity avagamyate / yadi vane 'nyena hetunā sadbhāvaviparītaḥ pratyaya utpadyate, mithyaiṣa vanapratyaya ity ato "vanaṃ nāsti" ity avagacchāmaḥ / na ca gavādiṣu pratyayo viparyeti / ato vaiṣamyam / atha
vanādiṣu naiva pratyayaviparyāsaḥ, na "te na santi" iti / tasmād asaṃbaddhaḥ paṅktivanopanyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If cognition of this kind arises even when there is no separate entity — as in 'a row,' 'a herd,' 'a forest' — [Reply:] No. This statement that has been adduced is irrelevant. Is the objection that direct perception itself is being challenged — 'even the trees do not exist' — by saying 'the cognition of a forest arises even when there is no forest'? If so, then the <s>Mahāyānika</s> (Mahāyāna Buddhist) position has [already] been refuted. Or is it the proponent of the reality of <s>ākṛti</s> (universal form) who is being criticized — 'your other thesis is flawed; even when there is no forest, the cognition of a forest would [wrongly] follow for you'? Even so, for one unable to refute the topic at hand, the criticism of another thesis constitutes a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>), because it is inconclusive. For he [the opponent of <s>ākṛti</s>] will say: 'Let it be flawed, if it is flawed; how does that flaw — or the absence of flaw — establish your thesis or refute my position?' And since no forest apart from trees is perceived, it is understood from that that 'the forest does not exist.' If the cognition of a forest arises from some other cause that is contrary to [its actual] existence, then this forest-cognition is false, and therefore we understand that 'the forest does not exist.' But the cognition regarding cows and the like does not go astray. Hence the dissimilarity. And if there is indeed no reversal of cognition in the case of forests and the like, then 'they do not exist' [does not follow]. Therefore, the citation of rows and forests is irrelevant.

body.text: ata upapannaṃ jaiminivacanam "ākṛtiḥ padārtha" iti / yathā ca ākṛtiḥ śabdārthas, tathopariṣṭān nipuṇataram upapādayiṣyāma iti /
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>Jaimini</s>'s statement — '<s>ākṛti</s> (universal form) is the meaning of a word' — is well-established. And how <s>ākṛti</s> is the meaning of a word, we shall establish more precisely later.

body.text: atha saṃbandhaḥ ka iti? - yat śabde vijñāte 'rtho vijñāyate /
body.translated_text: Now, what is the relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>)? — That by which, when a word is known, its meaning is known.

body.text: sa tu kṛtaka iti pūrvam upapāditam / tasmān manyāmahe kenāpi puruṣeṇa śabdānām arthaiḥ saha saṃbandhaṃ kṛtvā saṃvyavahartuṃ vedāḥ praṇītā iti /
body.translated_text: But that [relation] is artificial (<s>kṛtaka</s>), as was previously established. Therefore, we think that some person, having created the relation of words with their meanings, composed the <s>Vedas</s> for the purpose of conducting transactions.

body.text:
tad idānīm ucyate: apauruṣeyatvāt saṃbandhasya siddham iti / kathaṃ punar idam avagamyate "apauruṣeya eṣa saṃbandha" iti ?puruṣasya saṃbandhur abhāvāt / - kathaṃ saṃbandhā nāsti ? - pratyakṣasya pramāṇasya abhāvāt tatpūrvakatvāc cetareṣām / nanu ciravṛttatvāt pratyakṣasya aviṣayo bhaved idānīntanānām / na hi ciravṛttaḥ san na smaryeta / na ca himavadādiṣu kūpārāmādivad asmaraṇaṃ bhavitum arhati / puruṣaviyogo hi teṣu bhavati deśotsādena kulotsādena vā / na tu śabdārthavyavahāraviyogaḥ puruṣāṇām asti / - syād etat : saṃbandhamātravyavahāriṇo niṣprayojanaṃ kartṛsmaraṇam anādriyamānāḥ puruṣā vismareyur iti / - tan na / yadi hi puruṣaḥ kṛtvā saṃbandhaṃ vyavahārayet, vyavahārakāle 'vaśyaṃ smartavyo bhavet / saṃpratipattau hi kartṛvyavahartror arthaḥ sidhyati, na vipratipat tau / na hi vṛddhiśabdena apāṇiner vyavahārata ādaicaḥ pratiyeran pāṇinikṛtim ananumanyamānasya vā /
tathā makāreṇāpy apiṅgalasya na sarvagurus trikaḥ pratīyeta piṅgalakṛtim ananumanyamānasya vā / tena kartṛvyavahartārau saṃpratipadyete / tena vedair vyavaharadbhir avaśyam smaraṇīyaḥ saṃbandhasya kartā syād vyavahārasya ca / na hi vismṛte "vṛddhir ādaij" ity asya sūtrasya kartari "vṛddhir yasyācām ādis, tad vṛddham" iti kiṃcit pratīyeta / tasmād asmaraṇād avagacchāmaḥ ṅa kṛtvā saṃbandhaṃ vyavahārārthaṃ kenacid vedāḥ praṇītā" iti /
body.translated_text: To this it is now said: Because of the non-human origin (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the relation, it is established [that the <s>Veda</s> is authorless]. — But how is this understood, that 'this relation is non-human (<s>apauruṣeya</s>)'? — Because of the absence of a person [who created] the relation. — How is there no creator of the relation? — Because of the absence of perception as a valid means of knowledge, and because the other [means of knowledge] are preceded by it. — [Objection:] But because [the relation] has long been established, it may be beyond the perceptual range of people of the present. — [Reply:] That which has long been established would surely be remembered. Nor could there be non-remembrance [of the creator] as there is regarding wells, gardens, and the like with respect to the <s>Himālaya</s> and similar [places]. For in those cases, disconnection from persons occurs through the destruction of the land or the destruction of the lineage. But people are never disconnected from the transaction of words and meanings. — [Objection:] It might be that people, engaging merely in the transaction of the relation and finding no purpose in remembering the creator, would disregard [that memory] and forget. — [Reply:] No. For if a person, having created the relation, were to conduct transactions, the creator would necessarily be remembered at the time of transaction. For the purpose is fulfilled when both the creator and the user agree, not when they disagree. For without accepting <s>Pāṇini</s>'s authorship, one who does not follow <s>Pāṇini</s> would not understand the <s>āt</s>-substitution of <s>vṛddhi</s> from the [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>vṛddhir ādaic</s>.' Similarly, even from the syllable '<s>ma</s>,' one who is not [a student of] <s>Piṅgala</s> would not understand that every group of three [syllables beginning with '<s>ma</s>'] is heavy (<s>guru</s>), nor would one who does not accept <s>Piṅgala</s>'s authorship. Therefore, the creator and the user must agree. Therefore, those who use the <s>Vedas</s> must necessarily remember the creator of the relation and of the usage. For when the creator of the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vṛddhir ādaic</s>' is forgotten, nothing whatsoever would be understood — [namely,] that '<s>vṛddhi</s>' refers to those [vowels] whose initial is '<s>āi</s>.' Therefore, from the non-remembrance [of any creator], we understand that the <s>Vedas</s> were not composed by anyone having created the relation for the purpose of transaction.

body.text: yady api ca vismaraṇam upapadyeta, tathāpi na pramāṇam antareṇa saṃbandhāraṃ pratipadyemahi, yathā "vidyamānasyāpy anupalambhanaṃ bhavati" iti naitāvatā vinā pramāṇena śaśaviṣāṇaṃ pratipadyemahi / tasmād apauruṣeyaḥ śabdasyārthena saṃbandha iti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, even if forgetting were possible, still we would not accept a creator of the relation without a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), just as — even granting the principle that 'something that exists can sometimes be unperceived' — we would not on that account alone, without a <s>pramāṇa</s>, accept the existence of a hare's horn. Therefore, the relation of word with meaning is non-human (<s>apauruṣeya</s>).

body.text: nanv arthāpattyā saṃbandhāraṃ pratipadyemahi / na hi akṛtasaṃbandhāc chabdād arthaṃ pratipadyamānam upalabhāmahe / pratipadyeraṃs cet, prathamaśravaṇe 'pi pratipadyeran / tadanupalambhanād avaśyaṃ bhavitavyaṃ saṃbandhrā iti manyāmaha iti cet, - na /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But we would cognize the establisher of the relation [between word and meaning] through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). For we do not observe anyone understanding meaning from a word whose relation [with meaning] has not been established. If they could understand, they would understand even upon first hearing. Since that is not observed, there must necessarily be an establisher of the relation — so we think. — [Reply:] No.

body.text: siddhavad, upadeśāt / //
body.translated_text: [It is] as if [already] established, because of instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). //

body.text: yadi saṃbandhur abhāvān niyogato nārthā upalabhyeran, tato 'rthāpattyā saṃbandhāram avagacchāmaḥ / asti tv anyaḥ prakāraḥ / vṛddhānāṃ svārthena vyavaharamānānām upaśṛṇvanto bālāḥ pratyakṣam arthaṃ pratipadyamānā dṛśyante / te 'pi vṛddhā yadā bālā āsaṃs, tadā 'nyebhyo vṛddhebhyas, te 'py anyebhya iti nāsty ādir ity evaṃ vā bhavet / athavā na kaścid eko 'pi śabdo 'rthena saṃbaddha āsīt, atha kenacit saṃbandhāḥ pravartitā iti / atra vṛddhavyavahāre sati nārthād āpadyeta saṃbandhasya kartā / api ca vṛddhavyavahāravādinaḥ pratyakṣam upadiśanti, kalpayanti itare saṃbandhāram / na ca pratyakṣe pratyarthini kalpanā sādhvī / tasmāt saṃbandhur abhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: If meanings could absolutely not be grasped in the absence of the relation, then we would cognize the establisher of the relation through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). But there is another way. Children, overhearing elders conducting their affairs with [words having] their [established] meanings, are seen to directly understand the meaning. Those elders too, when they were children, [learned] from other elders, and those from yet others — thus there is no beginning; or alternatively, it may be that no single word was ever [originally] connected with a meaning, and then someone initiated the connections. In the case of establishment through the usage of elders, the maker of the relation would not be inferred from the object [through presumption]. Moreover, the proponents of establishment through elder-usage point to direct perception [as evidence], while the others [merely] postulate an establisher of the relation. And postulation is not valid when there is a counter-evidence from direct perception. Therefore, there is no establisher of the relation.

body.text: avyatirekaś ca //
body.translated_text: And [there is] non-deviation (<s>avyatireka</s>). //

body.text: yathā asmin deśe sāsnādimati gośabdaḥ, evaṃ sarveṣu durgameṣv api / bahavaḥ saṃbandhāraḥ kathaṃ saṃgamsyante / eko 'pi na śaknuyāt / ato nāsti saṃbandhā /
body.translated_text: Just as in this region the word '<s>go</s>' (cow) [is used] for [the animal] possessing a dewlap and the like, so too in all remote regions. How would many establishers [of the relation] have agreed [upon the same usage]? Even a single one could not [have accomplished it]. Therefore, there is no establisher of the relation.

body.text: apara āha
body.translated_text: Another says:

body.text: avyatirekaś ca //
body.translated_text: And [there is] non-deviation (<s>avyatireka</s>). //

body.text: na hi saṃbandhavyatiriktaḥ kaścit kālo 'sti, yasmin na kaścid api śabdaḥ kenacid arthena saṃbaddha āsīt / - katham ? - saṃbandhakriyaiva hi nopapadyate / avaśyam anena saṃbandhaṃ kurvatā kenacic chabdena kartavyaḥ / yena kriyeta, tasya kena kṛtaḥ? athānyena kenacit kṛtaḥ, tasya keneti, tasya keneti naivāvatiṣṭhate / tasmād avaśyam anena saṃbandhaṃ kurvatā akṛtasaṃbandhāḥ kecana śabdā vṛddhavyavahārasiddhā abhyupagantavyāḥ / asti ced vyavahārasiddhiḥ, na niyogataḥ saṃbandhā bhavitavyam ity arthāpattir api nāsti / - syād etat: aprasiddhasaṃbandhā bālāḥ kathaṃ vṛddhebhyaḥ pratipadyanta iti / - na hi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāma / dṛṣṭā hi bālā vṛddhebhyaḥ pratipadyamānāḥ, na tv apratipannasaṃbandhāḥ saṃbandhasya kartuḥ / tasmād vaiṣamyam /
body.translated_text: For there is no time whatsoever, apart from [the existence of] the relation, in which no word was connected with any meaning. — How so? — The very act of establishing a relation is impossible. For the person establishing the relation must necessarily employ some word [to do it]. By what [word] would it be done? Who established the relation of that [word]? If by some other [word], then who [established] that? And who [established] that? — there is no stopping point. Therefore, the person establishing the relation must necessarily accept that certain words, whose relations were not [deliberately] established, are established through the usage of elders. And if establishment through usage is [thus] admitted, then there need not necessarily be an establisher of the relation — so even the <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) [argument] does not hold. — [Objection:] It may be said: How do children, for whom the relation is not [yet] known, understand [meaning] from elders? — [Reply:] What is directly observed cannot be called impossible. For children are observed to understand [meaning] from elders, but an establisher of the relation who has not [himself first] understood the relation [is] not [observed]. Therefore, there is a disparity [between the two cases].

body.text: arthe 'nupalabdhe //
body.translated_text: When the object is not apprehended. //

body.text: anupalabdhe ca devatādāv arthe 'narthakaṃ saṃjñākaraṇam aśakyaṃ ca / viśeṣān pratipattuṃ hi saṃjñāḥ kriyante viśeṣāṃś coddiśya / tad viśeṣeṣv ajñāyamāneṣu ubhayam apy anavakḷptam / tasmād apauruṣeyaḥ śabdasya arthena saṃbandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: When the object — such as deities and the like — is not apprehended, the making of a conventional name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is both purposeless and impossible. For conventional names are made in order to communicate particular [things] and with reference to particular [things]. When the particulars are not known, both [the purpose and the possibility] are unaccomplished. Therefore, the relation of word with meaning is not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>).

body.text: ataś ca
body.translated_text: And therefore,

body.text: tat pramāṇam, anapekṣatvāt //
body.translated_text: That [Vedic word] is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), because of [its] independence (<s>anapekṣatva</s>). //

body.text: na hy evaṃ sati puruṣāntaraṃ pratyayāntaraṃ vā apekṣate / tasmāc codanālakṣaṇa eva dharmo nānyalakṣaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: For this being the case, it does not depend on any other person or any other cognition. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is characterized by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) alone and not by any other characterization.

body.text: bādarāyaṇagrahaṇam uktam /
body.translated_text: The mention of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> has been explained [above].

body.text: atha yad uktam "animittaṃ śabdaḥ ; karmakāle phalādarśanāt kālāntare ca karmābhāvāt pramāṇaṃ nāsti" iti, tad ucyate: na syāt pramāṇam, yadi pañcaiva pramāṇāny abhaviṣyan / yena yena hi pramīyate, tat tat pramāṇam / śabdenāpi pramīyate, tataḥ śabdo 'pi pramāṇam, yathaiva pratyakam / na ca pramāṇena avagatam, pramāṇāntareṇa anavagatam ity etāvatā anavagataṃ bhavati / na caivaṃ śrūyate "kṛte karmaṇi tāvaty eva phalaṃ bhavati", kiṃ tu "karmaṇā phalaṃ prāpyata" iti / - yac ca "kālāntare phalasya anyat pratyakkaṃ kāraṇam asti" iti, naiṣa doṣaḥ / tac caiva hi tatra kāraṇaṃ śabdaś ca iti /
body.translated_text: Now, as for what was said — "Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) has no ground; because the result is not seen at the time of the action, and because the action does not exist at a later time, there is no valid means [of knowledge]" — to that it is replied: It would not be a valid means of knowledge if there were only five means of valid knowledge. For whatever serves as a means by which [something] is known, that is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). By verbal testimony too [something] is known; therefore, verbal testimony too is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, just as perception is. And what is cognized by one <s>pramāṇa</s> does not become uncognized merely because it is not cognized by another <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor is it heard [in the Veda] thus: "When the action is performed, the result occurs at that very time." Rather, [it says:] "By the action, the result is obtained." As for [the objection] that "at a later time there is another directly perceived cause of the result" — this is not a fault. For that very [cause] is the cause there, and so too is verbal testimony [i.e., both serve as causes].

body.text: yat tu pratyakaviruddhaṃ vacanam upanyastaṃ śa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokaṃ yātīti pratyakṣaṃ śarīraṃ vyapadiśati" iti, tad ucyate: śarīrasaṃbandhād, yasya tac charīraṃ, so 'pi tair yajñāyudhair "yajñāyudhī" ity ucyate /
